# Summary: A Political Party Manifesto (2015)

## Overview

This document outlines a policy platform for a general election, presenting itself as an alternative to established political options. The manifesto emphasizes fiscal responsibility, controlled immigration, NHS investment, and withdrawal from the European Union as core priorities.

## Economic Policy

The manifesto proposes significant tax reforms including raising the personal allowance to £13,000 to exempt minimum wage earners from income tax, abolishing inheritance tax, and raising the 40% tax threshold to £55,000. Long-term goals include flattening income tax with rates of 20%, 30%, and 40%.

To reduce the deficit and national debt (cited at approximately £1.5 trillion), the plan proposes savings through leaving the EU (estimated £9 billion annually), reducing overseas aid from 0.7% to 0.2% of GNI, canceling the HS2 rail project (saving £4 billion), and reforming the Barnett Formula. The manifesto commits to eliminating the deficit by the parliament's third year.

Corporation tax reform focuses on closing loopholes that allow multinational corporations to pay minimal taxes by restoring tax sovereignty.

## Immigration

The document advocates for an Australian-style points-based immigration system, treating all nationalities equally. Key proposals include a five-year moratorium on unskilled worker immigration, establishing a Migration Control Commission, and limiting skilled work visas to 50,000 annually.

New migrants would require five years of tax contributions before accessing benefits or non-urgent NHS services. The manifesto emphasizes controlled borders while stating it welcomes beneficial immigration.

## Healthcare

The NHS would receive an additional £12 billion over five years, funding 8,000 more GPs, 20,000 additional nurses, and 3,000 midwives. Proposals include abolishing hospital parking charges, placing GPs in A&E departments, investing £130 million annually in dementia research, and improving mental health services.

The manifesto opposes "health tourism" and advocates charging non-eligible individuals for non-urgent treatment, requiring migrants to have medical insurance.

## Social Care and Welfare

Social care funding would increase by £1.2 billion annually to restore 2010 levels. The manifesto proposes abolishing the "bedroom tax," continuing housing benefit for under-25s, and increasing Carers' Allowance by £572 annually.

A Sovereign Wealth Fund from potential shale gas revenues is proposed to eventually fund elderly care costs, potentially implementing recommendations to cap individual care contributions.

## Education

The manifesto supports grammar schools, vocational education, and diverse school types. It proposes abolishing Key Stage 1 SATs, reducing teacher workloads, and waiving university tuition fees for students studying science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and medicine who subsequently work in the UK for five years.

## Housing and Environment

To address housing shortages, proposals include building one million homes on brownfield sites by 2025, offering grants and stamp duty exemptions for brownfield development, bringing empty homes back into use, and protecting greenbelt land from overdevelopment.

## Energy

The manifesto advocates repealing climate change legislation, withdrawing from EU emissions trading, and abolishing green taxes and levies on fuel bills. It supports shale gas exploration, coal industry revitalization, and renewable energy only where cost-competitive, while opposing wind farm subsidies.

## Employment and Small Business

Worker protection proposals include enforcing minimum wage laws, regulating zero-hours contracts, and allowing businesses to prioritize British citizens for employment. Small business support includes reducing business rates, addressing late payment issues, and cutting EU-derived regulations.

## Defense and Foreign Affairs

Defense spending would increase to meet NATO's 2% GDP requirement, with additional annual investment reaching £4 billion by 2020. The manifesto supports Trident nuclear deterrent renewal and opposes EU military integration.

Overseas aid would be reduced to 0.2% of GNI, focusing on emergency relief, healthcare, and clean water programs.

## Constitutional Reform

Proposed reforms include citizens' initiatives requiring referendums on petitions exceeding two million signatures, genuine recall powers for voters, confirmation hearings for ministerial appointments, and proportional representation voting reform.

## EU Withdrawal

The central policy commitment is holding an in/out referendum on EU membership, followed by orderly withdrawal using Article 50 of the Lisbon Treaty if voters choose to leave. Post-exit objectives include securing free trade agreements with the EU and other nations while maintaining cooperation on intelligence, extradition, and various cultural and scientific programs.
